title: An assigned embedded resolution is an affine descent of its own chart family
statement:
Fix a totally ordered label type $L$. Let $A$ be a rule on reduced finite-type rational schemes admitting a closed embedding in a smooth separated finite-type rational scheme [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data, def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule, def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. It assigns finite ordinary blowup towers with distinct increasing labels, coherent ideals with nonempty nowhere dense regular centers, and regular final scheme; its empty-input tower has length zero. For each open immersion of embeddable inputs over the rational base, its specified label-preserving cartesian contraction comparison deletes exactly the stages whose extended ideals are unit ideals [def-per-ordinary-tower-cartesian-map, def-nagata-extended-ideal, pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-regular-scheme].

Assume padded overlap compatibility as defined in [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data]. For every embeddable reduced finite-type rational input $S$ and every embeddability witness, its assigned tower $A(S)$ is an affine descent of $A$: there is a finite affine cover with embeddable coproduct total $T$ and a full labeled cartesian comparison over its covering map from $A(T)$ to $A(S)$, preserving every stage and the actual center ideals [def-trf-labeled-ordinary-zariski-resolution-data, def-per-ordinary-tower-cartesian-map].

proof.text: First check the domains of the constructions. The field $\mathbf Q$ is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and $\mathbf Q$), so $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open subscheme of $S$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. In particular an open immersion into $S$ is quasi-compact: its inverse image over any affine open of $S$ is another open subscheme of $S$. It is therefore of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and its source is of finite type over $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The same reasoning applies to affine opens inside intersections. Since $S$ is quasi-compact, [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open] gives a finite affine cover, including the empty cover when $S$ is empty.

source.place: VIII 2.1.4--2.1.9, 2.2.11, 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.5(ii), printed pp.87--88,91--92; explicit labeled Zariski-descent expansion.

proof.text: Each affine open $V$ used here is reduced by the local-ring definition [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra] its coordinate algebra is generated by finitely many elements over $\mathbf Q$. Sending variables to these generators presents it as $\mathbf Q[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/K$. Thus [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives a closed embedding $V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^r_{\mathbf Q}$. This ambient scheme is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], and of finite type by its polynomial coordinates. Consequently every such $V$ belongs to $\mathcal C$, and so do the finite disjoint unions of charts, by the stipulated closure of $\mathcal C$. In particular $A(U)$ and every $A(W)$ on an affine overlap are defined.

proof.text:
choose a finite affine open cover of the input S. The Noetherian finite-type
argument makes every chart a rational input, and a polynomial presentation of its
finite-type coordinate algebra embeds it in smooth separated affine space. The
finite disjoint union T of those charts is therefore embeddable. Compare the tower
A(S) to each chart by the rule's open comparison, and similarly compare A(T) to
each coproduct component. A label of A(S) occurs on some chart: otherwise its
extended ideal is unit on every lifted chart and therefore unit on its level,
contradicting its nonempty center. The same argument on T shows that a label of
A(T) occurs on some component chart. The chart towers are identical in these two
computations, so the two towers have the same ordered labels. Their full restrictions
on a chart are the same padded version of the assigned chart tower. Flat base change
supplies these full restrictions, with unit-ideal identity stages restored at exactly
the missing labels. At level zero the chart maps are the given inclusions into S.
Inductively, the center ideals pull back equally to the chart levels; the blowup
universal property gives the next level maps. Uniqueness of blowup lifts makes them
agree on overlaps. Assemble their disjoint union to obtain a cartesian map from
A(T) to A(S), retaining every label and center. It witnesses IsAffineDescent for
A(S). In the empty case both assigned towers have length zero and the same
construction uses the empty coproduct.

theorem embedded_resolution_isAffineDescent {L : Type w} [LinearOrder L]
    (A : OrdinaryZariskiResolutionRule.{u, w} L) (_hpad : A.HasPaddedOverlaps)
    (S : RationalResolutionInput.{u}) (hS : S.IsEmbeddable) :
    A.IsAffineDescent S (A.tower S hS)
